        inv_N = pow(N, MOD - 2, MOD)  # Modular inverse of N under modulo MOD
        expected_length = (total * inv_N) % MOD
        
        return expected_length
    
    # Calculate and print the result

def expected_lis_length():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    
    MOD = 1000000007
    
    N = int(data[0])
    A = list(map(int, data[1:N+1]))
    
    # Function to calculate the expected length of the longest increasing subsequence
    def lis_expected_length(A):
        # dp[i] will store the expected length of the longest increasing subsequence
        # ending at position i
        dp = [0] * N
        
        # Iterate over each position
        for i in range(N):
            # Start with the probability of 1 for the current element itself
            dp[i] = 1
            
            # Check all previous elements to update dp[i]
            for j in range(i):
                if A[j] < A[i]:
                    # If A[j] < A[i], we can extend the subsequence ending at j
                    dp[i] = (dp[i] + dp[j]) % MOD
        
        # The result is the average of the expected lengths of all subsequences
        total_probability = 1
        for i in range(N):
            total_probability = (total_probability * A[i]) % MOD
        
        # Calculate the expected length
        expected_length = sum(dp) * pow(total_probability, MOD - 2, MOD) % MOD
        
        return expected_length
